- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for high sentiment periods.
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 3.0), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 15–30% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for 3–5 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 3.0 and true outcome is < 2.5, adjust downward by 10–20%.
- For low sentiment + low price history, model underestimates; add 5–15% bias upward for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to lag; add 5–10% to forecast for 1–3 days to catch momentum.
- When sentiment is flat (0.50) or neutral, model often misses volatility; increase forecast variance by 10–20% for 3–5 days.
